prompt:
I need the front end for Pollsite Planner. An in-house planning tool a large county's elections department uses to assign polling places to precincts and assess candidate sites for distance, accessibility and capacity.

Who's using it: Rosa Delgado, polling place coordinator in the Maricopa-sized county's elections department. She has 11 years of experience, knows the county's precincts by heart, and works with the GIS analyst and the ADA compliance officer.

What they're doing right now: This morning Grace Fellowship Church, which hosts precincts 0412 and 0415 (about 6,900 registered voters combined), withdrew as a polling place for the 3 March 2027 presidential preference election because of a renovation. Rosa needs a replacement inside or close to those two precincts. It has to be within 1.5 miles for most voters, near a bus line, have at least 25 parking spaces with 2 accessible ones, and an accessible entrance. It also can't push voters across the six-lane arterial that splits the area, which caused complaints in 2022. She's comparing four candidate sites by where they sit relative to voters' homes and the arterial, then picking one to send for an ADA site survey. If none of them work, she'll try splitting the two precincts between two existing nearby sites.

What's in the system at this point: 412 precincts with boundaries and registered voter counts. 186 current polling places, each with address, capacity, accessibility survey date, parking counts and assigned precincts. Precinct 0412 has 3,840 voters and 0415 has 3,070. Four candidate sites: Desert Willow Elementary (gym, 1.1 mi from the centroid, 60 parking spaces, last surveyed 2023), Mesa Verde Community Center (0.8 mi, on the far side of the arterial), Saint Brendan's Parish Hall (1.6 mi, 28 spaces, survey pending), and Valley Branch Library (1.3 mi, 40 spaces, available only 7am–5pm). Also in the data: 3 bus routes with stops, the arterial road line, voter address density in clusters of about 50, and turnout from the 2024 general election (71%).

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
